label: Session 1 Notes
text: - Irreplaceable Agent Program Introduction: Brian St. Clair introduced the "Irreplaceable Agent" program, which is based on the premise that different agents win differently, either through systems, relationships, or speed. The training will not focus on national scripts but will be a system built around the individual agent's strengths. AI and the Industry Reality: Brian St. Clair noted that AI is causing job capabilities for mid-level production workers to be reduced, suggesting that agents using AI will replace those who do not. The program aims to address this by building a personalized system for each agent. Program Structure and Personalized Blueprint: The program structure includes seven weeks, covering topics such as how agents win, what moves the business, using AI the right way, building a personal system, and locking it in. The program uses the agent's Culture Index, past production, and social media activity to develop a personalized blueprint and prompts for AI, which will be delivered in a one-on-one meeting in Week five. Discussion on Market Activity: The discussion opened up to talk about current market activity, with one agent noting difficulty finding common ground with a luxury client over a small price difference, and another expressing satisfaction with their consistency, having closings every month this quarter. Competitive Buyer Market: Agents discussed working with buyers in Grapevine in the $500,000 to $600,000 price range, which is highly competitive, including a lost multiple offer situation that went $40,000 over asking with full appraisal waiver. Houses move fast and many are getting bought off market. Listing Updates and Challenges: Agents reported preparing a house for the market and working a listing in Mansfield that had been sitting for over 100 days despite price reductions, noting the need for updates and the lack of a pool as buyer feedback. Buyer Needs and Conclusion: Brian St. Clair confirmed they have multiple buyers who are not in a hurry, concluding the meeting and reminding everyone that a guest would cover the next part of the irreplaceable agent class.

label: Session 2 Notes
text: - Introduction to the Irreplaceable Agent Program: Brian St. Clair provided context for the "Irreplaceable Agent" program, explaining that the rapid development of artificial intelligence, particularly Claude AI, is expected to cause compression and potential elimination of 20 to 30% of mid-grade jobs across all industries. The program aims to help agents become irreplaceable by combining their natural "Culture Index" wiring (e.g., fast, systematic, big picture) with their past production data to develop a personalized blueprint of tasks and strategies. Understanding Individual Winning Styles: The core struggle for agents is trying to win the wrong way, often by attempting to emulate other agents. The program focuses on understanding how each agent naturally wins, such as moving fast and being relationship-driven, being systematic and detailed, or seeing the big picture and being opportunity-focused. When an agent understands their natural winning style, they stop fighting themselves and become more consistent. Identifying and Leveraging Natural Wiring: The three primary ways agents win are by being fast (action first), systematic (plan first), or strategic (observe first). Fast agents create momentum and trust, systematic agents create certainty and protect the deal, and strategic agents see the bigger picture and position the deal. Agents should know their primary style, which they should build their business around, acknowledging that most agents are a mix of two styles. The 6th Ave AI Playbook: A new resource called the "6th Ave AI playbook" is now available on the back site under the Irreplaceable Agent tab. This playbook contains a large collection of prompts that agents can run in AI for various situations, such as creating a full listing package, writing email subject lines, and creating open house posts. The playbook is intended to support the way agents work, not replace it, and will continue to be built out. Preparation for Future Sessions: Agents were instructed to pay attention over the next few weeks to when they feel most confident, when they feel stuck, what feels natural, and what feels forced to prepare for the one-on-one virtual blueprint session in week five. The goal is to build a system that aligns with their natural thinking and working style, as generic systems are the reason most agents remain inconsistent.

label: Session 3 Notes
text: - The Agent's Evolving Value in the Age of AI: Brian St. Clair framed the agent's role as shifting away from being a mere information provider, which AI can easily do. The real value of an agent is now in helping clients navigate fear, confusion, timing, and pressure to make wise decisions, which cannot be commoditized. Decisions as the Core Agent Function: The agent's job is not information but decisions, such as determining the right house, real price, and the wisdom of negotiating versus walking away from issues. Decisions live in the specifics of the client's unique situation, while information like mortgage rates or market trends is readily available everywhere. AI Limitations and Agent Superpowers: Brian St. Clair highlighted specific situations, like identifying mold or recognizing neighborhood premiums, where agent experience and pattern recognition prevail over AI. The emotional component and psychological influence an agent provides, such as managing a seller's reaction to negotiation, are also areas where AI cannot replace human judgment. Decision-Making for Agent Success: Agents were categorized based on their strengths (Fast, Systematic, and Strategic) and experience levels, noting that new agents win with responsiveness, while experienced agents win with judgment and leverage. Buyers' main fear is making the wrong decision, and agents lose deals through indecision, not lack of effort. AI as a Tool for Better Decisions: Brian St. Clair reiterated that AI cannot replace the agent's decision-making ability but can serve as a leverage point by supporting better and quicker decisions. One agent demonstrated using a dictation app during showings to brain dump and organize thoughts for client recap emails, highlighting how AI can improve process quality and organization. The AI Playbook and Future Outlook: Brian St. Clair showed the team the 6th Ave AI Playbook, which contains customizable prompts for various tasks, like summarizing title commitments and creating social media posts. Brian warned that compression is coming and encouraged agents to use AI as an assistant to stay ahead.

label: Session 4 Notes
text: - AI and the Core Value of Innovation: Brian St. Clair reiterated the core value of rejecting the status quo, noting that industry compression is occurring across fields, including real estate, due to AI. G Suite now has integrated AI, and the team shared positive feedback on using Grok and Claude for different tasks, such as generating graphic material. Getting Ahead of the AI Curve: The discussion emphasized the need to get ahead of the AI curve. The goal of the class is to amplify agents through AI, not replace them. AI acts as a friction remover and pattern recognizer, handling volume so agents can focus on what matters. AI for Creative Property Descriptions: Brian St. Clair shared an example of using Claude and ChatGPT to rewrite property descriptions as a story, which they found to be a more effective strategy than standard MLS descriptions. Amplifying Strengths with AI: Agents who use AI to amplify their strengths become unstoppable, while those who use it to avoid thinking lose their edge. The competitive advantage lies in knowing how to use AI strategically, which is based on understanding one's own winning style (relationship builder, deal master, or opportunity spotter). AI for Relationship Building and Deal Management: For agents who win through relationships, AI can remove the friction of what to say by generating conversational openers and suggesting who to reach out to. For those who win by managing deals, AI can help identify next steps, urgent issues, and potential deal-breakers by analyzing current deal statuses and associated documents. Listing Management and Strategy: An example was provided where Claude analyzed new listing pictures and asked if the sellers were still stuck at 825, demonstrating AI's ability to provide strategic feedback. The idea of refreshing a listing's description through AI every two weeks was mentioned, along with the effectiveness of using Instagram videos to generate leads. AI for Opportunity Spotting: For agents who win by seeing opportunities, AI can help identify what they might be missing in the current market and pipeline by analyzing deals and market trends. The overall pattern for using AI is that the agent thinks, AI organizes, the agent decides, AI supports, and the agent adjusts. Real-World AI Use Case (Inspection Negotiation): Jamie shared a real-world use case of using Claude to manage a buyer's inspection request: inputting the inspection report and buyer requests, asking AI for estimated costs, and requesting a draft response outlining what to say yes and no to. AI also helped comb through seller receipts and virtual tour screenshots to identify a specific replacement tile and estimate the needed quantity, ultimately helping draft a multi-option PDF and communication emails for the client. Real-World Use Case (Lowball Offers): Jamie also shared a strategy of advising clients with large budgets to target houses that have been on the market for a long time and submit lowball offers. This strategy has been successful, with one client getting a house $200,000 off the current price and $300,000 off the original list price. Buyers should focus on properties listed for more than two weeks for the best opportunity.

label: Session 5 Notes
text: Systemization and AI Integration: The Irreplaceable Agent blueprint was launched to systematize operations and AI usage. The group decided to prioritize private data security by prohibiting input of sensitive client information. AI Integration and Workflow Impact: Brian St. Clair discussed the evolution of AI, specifically citing the release of Claude AI by Anthropic and the introduction of AI agents. AI is driving industry compression by automating tasks previously requiring significant human labor, such as auditing website code or reviewing long documents. The strategy is to use AI to improve communication, strategy, and decision-making for specific client situations rather than asking general questions. Business Systemization and Blueprints: Brian St. Clair argued that top agents rely on repeatable systems rather than relying solely on memory or motivation. A blueprint approach helps identify personal operating styles, decision-making triggers, and consistent follow-up processes. The Irreplaceable Agent System: Brian St. Clair described the Irreplaceable Agent system as a non-generic operating system tailored to each individual's Culture Index, past production, and personality. The system includes a decision framework, an AI engine, daily non-negotiables, and a feedback loop intended to reduce guesswork in daily business operations. AI Customization and Public Proof: Brian St. Clair emphasized that the system helps agents define their unique value proposition. He discussed the importance of public proof, noting that detailed reviews mentioning an agent's specific niche, such as being a move-up buyer agent, are becoming AI-readable trust signals that help AI connect clients with the right agents. AI Security and Privacy Concerns: An agent raised questions regarding the security of client information when using AI. Brian St. Clair responded that private client information, such as names or sensitive data, should not be input into AI platforms. He clarified that he personally uses Claude on a standalone machine and does not have settings enabled that allow data to be used for crowdsourced training, keeping information within his private account. System Implementation and Conclusion: Brian St. Clair provided instructions on setting up AI by creating personas, such as strategist, philosopher, and architect, to ensure the AI responds in a way that matches the user's voice and thinking pattern. He concluded by encouraging the team to implement the blueprint system immediately to begin seeing results within two to three months, with next week's meeting focusing on vision and future growth.

label: Session 6 Notes
text: - Business Vision and Alignment: Brian St. Clair stated that agents often suffer from burnout because they lack a defined vision for the type of business they want to build, leading to reactive and exhausting growth. The solution is to use AI to interview oneself about goals and strengths to create a clear, intentional business model. Irreplaceable Agent System: Brian St. Clair emphasized that the Irreplaceable Agent blueprint provided to participants is designed specifically for them, as opposed to generic corporate systems, and encouraged everyone to run the system to see results within 30 days. Competing on Judgment: Brian St. Clair argued that agents should compete on their judgment rather than social media followers, as AI is becoming a standard tool for clients to find and evaluate agents. Extreme Ownership and AI Success: Brian St. Clair cited the week 7 core value of extreme ownership for successes and failures, sharing that he personally secured two listings this week from clients who found him via ChatGPT using his established blueprint. Consistency and Execution: Brian St. Clair reinforced that business rewards execution and consistency rather than just the acquisition of knowledge from classes, and encouraged participants to time-block their tasks to ensure they are actively running their systems. Future Developments and Conclusion: Brian St. Clair announced plans to rebuild the company website and back-end systems within the next three to five months and confirmed that they are developing a new agent onboarding system.

label: Align Your AI — Start Here
text: Before You Use Your Blueprint: Align Your AI to How You Actually Win. Most agents use AI like a search engine. They ask random questions, get generic answers, then decide AI doesn't really work. That's not the problem. The problem is that AI doesn't understand how they think, communicate, make decisions, solve problems, build relationships, or operate their business. AI becomes exponentially more useful when it understands how you naturally win, what slows you down, how you communicate, where you create value, what kind of clients you work best with, and how you actually make decisions in real life. High performers do not use AI for information alone. They use AI for leverage. Before using your Blueprint, spend 20 to 30 minutes helping your AI understand how you operate. Do not skip this. Otherwise, AI will continue giving generic output because it still thinks you are generic. The 7-Step AI Alignment Process. 1. Tell AI Who You Are: Interview me to understand how I naturally win in real estate, how I communicate, what energizes me, what drains me, and how I make decisions. 2. Explain Your Business: your market, your price point, your clients, your schedule, your goals, and how your business actually operates. Not the business you wish you had, the business you actually run right now. Context compounds. 3. Explain Your Strengths: relationships, organization, analysis, negotiation, systems, consistency, leadership, communication, creativity, strategy, and follow-through. 4. Show AI Where You Need Leverage: overthinking, inconsistency, follow-up hesitation, organization, distraction, perfectionism, overwhelm, difficult conversations, starting conversations, and closing conversations. 5. Teach AI Your Voice: Paste in emails, texts, listing descriptions, client updates, social posts, and negotiation messages. Then tell AI to learn how you naturally communicate and write in your voice. 6. Give AI a Role: Rainmaker to deal strategist, momentum coach, opportunity finder. Coordinator to execution assistant, organization partner, clarity builder. Philosopher to strategist, pattern analyst, leverage advisor. Socializer to relationship coach, conversation assistant, follow-up partner. Specialist to technical advisor, deal analyst, expertise amplifier. 7. Use One Thread Consistently: Do not start over every day. Create dedicated threads for each listing, each buyer, negotiations, inspection reports, title commitments, pricing strategy, content, marketing, follow-up, and strategy. Then continue using those same threads over time. Context compounds. Final Reminder: Your Blueprint is not designed to replace your judgment. It is designed to help AI understand how you think, communicate, decide, and operate so it can support you more effectively. You'll know it's working when AI responses start sounding less generic and more specific to your actual deals, clients, communication style, and decision-making process.

label: AI Aligned Testimonial Email
text: The AI Testimonial Review Email. Howdy [client name]! Now that you're a few months settled into the home, congrats again! It was truly a pleasure helping you through the process. As you know, my business is built almost entirely through referrals and relationships, so honest feedback from great clients like you means a lot to me. One thing that's changing quickly in real estate is how people search for agents online. More buyers and sellers are using Google, AI tools, and review sites to figure out who actually communicates well, solves problems, negotiates effectively, and takes care of people during the process. Because of that, detailed and honest reviews matter more than ever. If you'd be willing, I'd sincerely appreciate a quick review about your experience working with me. A few things that are especially helpful for people reading reviews: how communication felt during the transaction, what stood out about the process, how problems or surprises were handled, whether you felt informed and protected, and anything you think made the experience different from past transactions. Of course, only share what honestly reflects your experience. Here are a couple of places you could leave a review: Google, Zillow, Realtor. I truly appreciate your support and the trust you placed in me throughout the process. As a small thank you, just shoot me a quick text or email after you leave the review and I'll send a gift card your way! By the way, if you know of anyone that is buying or selling and would appreciate the level of service that I provide, would you give me a call with their name and number? I will be happy to follow up and take extra special care of your friends and family. Thanks again!

label: Commitment — Slides
text: Irreplaceable Agent — Commitment. This is where it becomes real. 6th Ave Homes Core Value 12: We take extreme ownership for both the success and failure of any project and role we are tasked with. Success is always our individual responsibility and we do not place blame elsewhere when mistakes are made. Ownership requires humility, vulnerability, and self-awareness as these are the foundation of good leadership. Let's Be Honest: You've heard a lot. You've had some ideas. You've seen what can work. But none of that matters if you don't use it. This Is What Happens: Agents learn things. They get motivated. They say this makes sense. And then they go right back to the same habits. Be Honest With Yourself: How many times have you learned something that made sense, felt motivated, said I'm going to do this, and didn't follow through? Not because it was wrong. Not because it wasn't helpful. Because you didn't run it. That's the Whole Game: This business doesn't reward what you know. It rewards what you actually do. You Already Know Enough: You are not missing information. You know how you win. You know where you get paid. You know how to use AI to support it. You're Missing One Thing: Consistency. That's Why Your Blueprint is Different: It fits you. Which means you can actually run it. So Here's the Truth: If you run your system, your business improves. If you don't, nothing changes. That's not opinion. That's how this works. The Standard: A 6th Ave Irreplaceable Agent understands how they win, builds around it, and uses clarity and AI to serve clients at a level that can't be replaced. The Decision: You don't need more time. You don't need more information. You already know what to do. This either becomes how you work, or it doesn't. That's the difference.
